R28-2b (docs/REINTERP_R28-2_GUIDED_NARRATIVE_SPEC_2026-07-10.md §3, the tapes): three cassette props on the Room 1 bookcase shelf, played through the boombox (src/narrative/tapes.ts owns the state machine + witness filing; src/engine/app.ts wires the physical click + the room-caption DOM + audio). Segments are `{ id, at, caption, kind, audio }` — `at` is seconds from PLAY start (ambient playback advancing captions on its own clock, NOT a player-facing deadline — no scrubbing/progress UI exists, per the click/tap law); `audio` optionally names a bundled filename registered in src/audio/tapeAudio.ts's registry — an unregistered name is simply never requested (no console error). DEGRADATION DOCTRINE (docs/REINTERP_AUDIO_PRODUCTION_GUIDE_2026-07-11.md §4, binding): every real filename referenced below is the DEGRADED (`_tape97`-suffixed) master generated by tools/degrade_audio.sh from the pristine original in assets/audio/ — SYSTEM audio stays clean elsewhere in the piece, but audio heard as coming off one of THESE physical tapes is always degraded first. WITNESS SYMMETRY (binding, ERA_MINING FIND #4, R28-2 spec §3/§6): Tape A and Tape B file 'playedThrough' (reached the tail after their last segment) or 'stoppedMidway' (play started — elapsedSec > 0 — then stopped/ejected/era-shifted before the tail) to ledger.tapes; a tape that is never pressed to PLAY (inserting it alone does not count) files NOTHING. Tape C (the mixtape) carries NO `witness` field at all (null) and src/narrative/tapes.ts enforces in CODE, not just by omitting data here, that it never reaches ledger.tapes and never sets the 'tape-played' ledger record the guide's `tape` side-message (s1_guide.json) waits on. cutting/beat metadata per the rails. TIMING NOTE (Session 32): Tape A's prayer captions and Tape C's track-1 captions are DERIVED from Sérgio's delivered lyric sheets (Fold My Hands.txt has no timestamps — captions are evenly distributed across the real ffprobe'd duration, approximate by design; family_design_solutions.txt and discover_the_new_you.txt carry word-level LRC timestamps, grouped line-by-line into captions, so those two are precisely synced to the real audio; a small handful of ties/out-of-order timestamps in the source LRC — flagged inline — were resolved by hand). Fine-grained resync is a polish pass, not blocking.
